authoredPrompt: This figure traces the operation of merge sort on an eight-element array as a bottom-up lattice of gray boxes linked by thick gray arrows. The bottom rank, tagged "initial sequence", holds eight single-element squares reading 5, 2, 4, 7, 1, 3, 2, 6 from left to right. Pairs of arrows, each pair captioned "merge", lift adjacent squares into four two-element boxes reading 2 5, 4 7, 1 3, and 2 6. A second rank of merge arrows combines those into two four-element boxes, 2 4 5 7 and 1 2 3 6. A last pair of arrows, again captioned "merge", brings both into the wide box at the top, tagged "sorted sequence", which reads 1 2 2 3 4 5 6 7. Box width scales with the run it holds, so the doubling of sorted-run length shows up directly as the boxes widen from rank to rank while their count halves. Read upward, the drawing presents the algorithm as repeated merging of already-sorted runs.
authoredInteractions:
- Code editor for merge(left, right): learner implements the merge routine with compare-front, append, and advance primitives for the shown sorted runs; running the code moves values into the active output box one comparison at a time.
- Step through merge-sort calls: the active pair of boxes, merge arrow, and destination run highlight as the recursive merge tree builds from singletons to the final sorted sequence.
- Toggle stable-merge trace: duplicate 2 values keep their relative order while the code runs, making stability visible instead of only showing the final sorted row.

Figure 2.4 illustrates the operation of the procedure bottom-up when n is a power of 2. The algorithm consists of merging pairs of 1-item sequences to form sorted sequences of length 2, merging pairs of sequences of length 2 to form sorted sequences of length 4, and so on, until two sequences of length n=2 are merged to form the final sorted sequence of length n.

discrepancies: Arrowheads are disproportionately large and overlap the destination boxes, whereas the source uses standard-sized arrowheads
The initial sequence boxes have uniform horizontal spacing, missing the pair-based visual grouping (wider gaps between pairs) seen in the source
The default visual state upon loading leaves the upper tree levels empty pending user code execution, whereas the source figure shows the completed, fully-populated sort
evaluation.notes: An exceptionally pedagogical interactive workbench that actually executes and traces user-written merge sort code, though the default visual state diverges from the source due to oversized arrowheads and starting empty.
action_items: Fix the giant arrowheads: in SVG.js, markers scale with line stroke-width by default. Add `.attr('markerUnits', 'userSpaceOnUse')` to the marker definitions, or significantly shrink the drawn marker polygon.
Adjust the level 0 node layouts to group the initial sequence into pairs (e.g., [5, 2] gap [4, 7]), matching the spatial grouping of the source figure.

Pre-select the 'Correct' code snippet and automatically call `window.runCode()` on initialization so the figure defaults to a fully populated state matching the source image, while still leaving the interactive workbench functional.
